truth_source: per-language LSP reference server on a real public repository (callHierarchy preferred, references+documentSymbol enclosure fallback)
truth_filter: both sides restricted to textually-defined callers; macro/codegen-expanded caller names (no textual definition in the repo) excluded and listed per symbol
scoring: deterministic simple-name set comparison; no LLM
corroboration: where the two tools disagree, the source text adjudicates, and every excusal is listed per symbol. extras_reference_blind (all languages): an Atlas-only caller with a proven CALL SITE of the probe inside its own documentSymbol span is a reference-server blind spot, not a false positive. The site must be call-shaped in a spelling the language makes statically unambiguous (see corroboration_shapes) and must survive comment/string blanking — a name merely MENTIONED corroborates nothing. missed_reference_coarse (opt-in, see corroboration_languages): a truth-only caller whose body never mentions the probe in ANY shape — qualified, parenless, piped or captured — cannot be a textual call site, so it leaves the recall denominator (truth_scored) while truth_callers keeps the server's raw count. The two probes differ in strictness by design: crediting Atlas demands a proven call site, excusing Atlas is triggered by absence of evidence and so uses the widest possible net over the RAW text. A probe whose reference callers are ALL refuted measures nothing and is dropped from scoring and listed under unscorable_probes with both tools' answers.

macro_only_excluded: given an editorconfig containing a certain property with a non-default value and add the same property again with default value then the non-default value is not overwritten
given an editorconfig containing a property for which a property mapper is defined then the property mapper is called
given an editorconfig containing some properties then mapping of all properties is possible
given an editorconfig from which a deprecated -error-level- property is retrieved then thrown an exception
given an editorconfig from which a deprecated -warning-level- property is retrieved then do not throw an exception
given an editorconfig to which properties are added with the same name but different identities than those properties can not be loaded in the same editorconfig
given an editorconfig with a defined code style and add a property with default value then the default value can be retrieved for the default code style
given an empty editorconfig and add a property with default value then the default value can be retrieved for the default code style
given that the output has to be colored
